title: Thistle Well on‑prem LLM integration backlog
content:
Quick context:
Customer: Thistle Well (small chain of specialty clinics) — wants an on‑prem/private deployment for patient data privacy and intermittent connectivity. They asked for a multi‑tenant setup inside their datacenter with a Redwood private control plane agent (air‑gapped allowed).

Call notes (2026-02-12) — capture highlights and verbatim fragments:
- Customer: "No outbound allowed except to our internal vault and SSO provider."
- Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA A40 per cluster node, slow SAN (2x 10Gb iSCSI) with latency spikes in the morning window.
- Expected RPS: 15–25 concurrent inference requests for the first phase, spiky batch jobs during nightly summarization.
- Required SLA: 99.95 for read latency, business needs sub‑200ms median per token for chat flows.
- Compliance: HSM for keys (Yubico / Thales), audit logs must be exportable to their SIEM (Splunk).
- Integration: message bus is RabbitMQ; they prefer event‑driven routing rather than direct HTTP.
- Failover: they want the ability to fallback to Redwood Hosted for non‑PHI requests during maintenance windows (but outbound constraints make this tricky).

Technical requirements (raw):
- Private control plane/agent that can operate in an air‑gapped network or via a one‑way egress proxy (customer prefers the egress proxy pattern).
- KMS/HSM integration (customer uses Thales Luna). Need documentation for CA cert import and key policy mapping.
- Per‑tenant model pinning and isolation; ability to restrict access to model catalog per tenant.
- Disk-backed KV cache vs in‑memory: given SAN latency, we must provide guidance on local NVMe cache or an option to tune cache eviction to avoid hot reads on SAN.
- Quantization: customer wants 4-bit inference if accuracy acceptable. Need a short eval plan (dataset subset) to measure regressions vs fp16.
- Observability: token‑level latency breakdown (ingest, queuing, kernel time), plus audit events for every model run.
- Network: L4 firewall rules require a list of egress IPs for the agent; provisioning team will need a small, immutable CIDR list.
- Storage: model artifacts will be pre‑staged via secure USB drive on the appliance (air‑gap). We must provide md5/sha256 checks and signed manifests.

Gotchas / risk register (things to surface ASAP):
- SAN latency: KV cache thrashing if we rely on NFS for latent KV store. Recommend local NVMe cache node or pinned local disk for runtime.
- A40 memory: per‑model KV footprint tests needed — if context windows > 8k they might run out of GPU memory with KV caching enabled.
- HSM integration operational friction: Thales key rotation policy requires agent restart unless we implement a hot‑reload flow. Might need a small change in our agent.
- No outbound policy: prevents Hosted fallback unless customer allows a specific egress channel during maintenance; otherwise fallback must be strictly within cluster (so implement model variant fallback).
- RabbitMQ backpressure: their event expiry is short (30s). We need fast acking strategy and a small worker pool to avoid message drops.
- Nightly summarization: large batching jobs risk starving low‑latency traffic if autoscaling boundaries are not tuned.

Immediate next steps (prioritized):
1) Security/arch deep dive (owner: Priya) — verify HSM onboarding steps and whether Thales Luna supports our agent hot key reload. Ticket: PS-4024 (in intake backlog). Target: 2026-02-22.
2) SRE perf probe (owner: Caleb) — run KV/local NVMe proof‑of‑concept on a 2x A40 node with simulated SAN latency patterns. Produce perf report (latency histogram per token). Ticket: ENG-7581. Target: 2026-02-28.
3) Network provisioning doc (owner: Maya) — produce minimal egress CIDR list + port list for their firewall team. Include fallback recipe if outbound blocked. Deliverable: short one‑pager. Target: 2026-02-18 (done draft) — follow up to confirm acceptance.
4) Quantization eval (owner: Diego) — create small eval harness (1000 clinical Q/A pairs anonymized) to test 4-bit vs fp16 LAT and quality. Provide clear acceptance criteria (<= 2% drop in top‑1 accuracy for structured outputs). Target: 2026-03-05.
5) Message bus adapter sketch (owner: Maya) — show how Redwood agent will subscribe to RabbitMQ, ack semantics, and dead‑letter handling. Include recommended prefetch and worker pool sizes (start: prefetch=16, workers=8). Target: 2026-02-20.

Notes to self / shorthand TODOs:
- TODO: check if agent can mount USB pre‑staged model dir read‑only (security asks for mount with nosuid,nodev).
- TODO: sample conn string for Splunk ingestion (customer wants a secure forwarder).
- Follow up with sales: clarify commercial for HSM integration (cost + SLA delta).
- Draft fallback policy: prefer model variant fallback first; only attempt hosted fallback if customer explicitly enables a one‑time egress window.

Customer concerns to address explicitly in next call:
- Will local NVMe be acceptable to Thistle Well procurement? If not, discuss licensing for a small SSD bundle.
- Clarify exact key rotation schedule for Thales (monthly vs quarterly).
- Confirm whether PHI will ever be sent to Hosted fallback (we should get a hard NO; if yes, require DLP).

Meeting cadence proposal:
- Weekly 30m standups (Thu 10:00 PT) for first 6 weeks, then shift to biweekly after POC.
- Ad‑hoc tech deep dives with Priya/Caleb as needed.

Useful quick links / refs:
- Confluence intake (linked above).
- Internal playbook: Private deploy HSM checklist (search: private-deploy/hsm-checklist).
- Perf script: scripts/kv-probe-a40.sh (ENG repo).

Open questions (for engineering review):
- Can runtime hot‑reload keys from HSM without full agent restart?
- How bad is the GPU memory increase with local NVMe KV vs pure in‑GPU KV for long contexts?
- Do we have a clean customer‑facing wording for "fallback to Hosted" that covers air‑gap constraints?

End of scratchpad — keep this file as the canonical user notes for Thistle Well POC. Will spin a cleaned summary for the customer once the perf probe returns (target draft: 2026-03-08).
